# `query_record` pipeline DSL

`steps` is a non-empty pipeline folded left to right over a working set. The first step must be a filter. Each later filter narrows the current set; each traversal replaces it with selected neighbours.

## Filter step

Use `{"step":"filter", ...}`. Populated fields are ANDed; list values are any-of. The exact selectors are `ids`, `types`, `kinds`, `home_id`, `ancestor_id`, `lifecycle`, `maturity`, `persistence`, `owner_id`, `bears_shape`, `has_query`, `facets`, `name_contains`, `updated_since`, `last_activity_since`, and `include_archived`. `home_id` is direct placement; `ancestor_id` is a subtree. Names are case-insensitive substrings, and both time selectors are inclusive RFC 3339 lower bounds. There is no before-time predicate.

An empty filter is the explicit all-visible-records starting set. One facet object is `{"key":"priority"}` for existence, or has one of `value`, `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `lte`, `gt`, `gte`, `in`, `lt_facet`, `lte_facet`, `gt_facet`, or `gte_facet`. `value` is the legacy exact-string form (`null` means existence); `eq` and `ne` take strings. Ordered JSON numbers use the numeric lane, ordered strings compare lexicographically, and each `in` item selects its lane. A single same-lane lower-plus-upper pair is also valid, for example `{"key":"score","gte":0.5,"lt":1}`. Facet-to-facet operators take the other facet key and compare numeric lanes on the same record. Preserve JSON numbers for numeric comparisons.

`include_archived` belongs to each filter step; traversal does not itself remove archived neighbours. If archived endpoints must be excluded, add a filter step after the traversal with the desired archive policy instead of assuming the starting filter carries through.

## Traverse step

Use `{"step":"traverse","target":"links|children|parents", ...}`. The exact targets are `links`, `children`, and `parents`. Link traversal may set one `relationship` and `direction` to `out`, `in`, or `both` (the default); child and parent traversal use the containment tree. Traversals are set operations under caller visibility and do not mutate links or homes.

## Terminal shape

Without a count or aggregate terminal, results are records. `limit` defaults to 50, has range 1–500, and `offset` defaults to zero and must be non-negative. `order` is exactly `updated_desc` (default), `created_desc`, `last_activity_desc`, or `name_asc`. `facet_order` has shape `{"key":"score","lane":"number","direction":"desc"}`; lane is `number|text`, direction is `asc|desc`, missing values sort last, ordinary `order` is secondary, and record ID is the final ascending tie-break.

`count_by` is exactly `type`, `kind`, `lifecycle`, `maturity`, `persistence`, or `facet`; `facet` requires the top-level `facet_key`, and other axes reject it. Count terminals reject `facet_order`.

`aggregate` is `{"op":"count"}` or a numeric facet fold such as `{"op":"avg","facet_key":"score"}`. Operations are exactly `count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, and `max`. `count` forbids `facet_key`; all others require a non-empty one. Aggregate terminals reject `count_by`, the top-level count `facet_key`, `order`, `facet_order`, `limit`, and `offset`.

Optional `as_of` is exactly one of `{"content_seq":123}` with a non-negative sequence or `{"timestamp":"2026-08-03T12:00:00Z"}` with an RFC 3339 timestamp. It pins the content projection; current schema, vocabulary, and retained blob metadata remain live.

Use `get_record` for a known full id or short record reference, `search` for free text, `scan` for cross-axis orientation, and `query_sql` when the needed relational expression is outside this grammar.
